name: windows-safe-terminal-input

test_list.description: Native C0 Enter retains Shift as a modifier.
Native Ctrl+Enter retains Control and is not classified as Shift+Enter.
C0 key records with virtual key zero map to printable control-key events.
Win32 repeat counts and key-up records retain Crossterm event phases.
Adjacent UTF-16 surrogate records decode into one Unicode scalar.
Bracketed paste payload retains escape sequences literally and emits one paste event.
Native paste payloads above one MiB are rejected with bounded state.
A stop token ends Crossterm polling immediately and unknown capability remains unknown.
Terminal output and keyboard mode attempts are paired with restoration.
Native VT cursor and function key sequences normalize into events.
CSI-u Shift+Enter and modified arrow keys preserve their key and modifier semantics.
CSI-u Ctrl+Enter and SGR hover bytes normalize as events and do not leak into composer text.
Track the right-button state across native press/release records so release reports Right rather than defaulting to Left.
Track the middle-button state across native press/release records so release reports Middle rather than defaulting to Left.
Preserve a left drag while tracking a right-button press and left/right releases by the exact single changed button.
Do not assign an ambiguous simultaneous button transition to an arbitrary button; synchronize state so a later single transition retains identity.
A Windows ConPTY Shift+Enter inserts a draft row and Shift+Up keeps the physical cursor on the draft row.
A prompt in --demo runs scripted local behavior without session state writes.
F5 switches profiles and mouse hover input remains an event.
Native LF input maps back to Ctrl+J while CR remains Enter.
ConPTY delayed Unicode on VK_MENU, VK_LMENU, or VK_RMENU key-up becomes a single text press; ordinary key-up remains a release.
A bounded fixture sends $ and ASCII keys through ConPTY and verifies native console key records preserve their Unicode values.
A typed directive beginning with $ remains intact through native ConPTY input and commits.
A bracketed paste beginning with $ remains literal and is not submitted.
After the one-MiB limit is exceeded, payload tail is discarded through the paste end marker; only later input is emitted.

inputs.name: Windows INPUT_RECORD key event
inputs.description: Virtual key, UTF-16 code unit, modifier bits and repeat/down state.

inputs.name: native normalized events
inputs.description: Bounded stream of native key, mouse, resize and focus events.

inputs.name: terminal mode snapshot
inputs.description: Exact input and output modes captured before changes.

output_type: normalized terminal input and restored console state
output_description: Shift+Enter remains distinguishable from Ctrl+Enter; bracketed paste is literal and capped at one MiB; input polling is bounded and cancellable. CSI-u keyboard and SGR mouse input is decoded through the native Windows path. Native key-up Alt composition records that carry translated Unicode are normalized to one Press without duplicating ordinary key-up text. Once an oversized paste is rejected, all remaining payload is discarded through the end marker before input resumes.
